answer: Peer-mapped diversity quota: before an identity can attest, it must place itself on the network atlas by proving connectivity to peers spread across regions, and any two nodes whose paths share one origin are merged on the map. Sybil farms collapse into a single dot with one vote. An orchard works the same way: every tree grafted from one rootstock shares its fate, so cloning many trunks from one root yields one harvest, not many. Attestation travels like a voyage: claims reach consensus by hopping through distant, independent witnesses, and clones cannot both stand on one route.
